## Miguel Cosenza Contreras

Proteomics Data Scientist | Computational Biologist | Multi-omics Translational Data Science | Statistical Programmer\
Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany  
[migueljcc5@gmail.com](mailto:migueljcc5@gmail.com) | [GitHub](https://github.com/MiguelCos) | [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9727-3229) | [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=DbsUEGsAAAAJ&hl) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/miguel-cosenza-contreras-972414114/)

## Profile

Proteomics data scientist, computational biologist, and statistical programmer with a PhD in Biology, developing computational tools and reproducible analytical solutions for multidisciplinary life-science research. I connect biological questions with statistical reasoning, informatics, and automation, translating shared analytical decisions into workflows for data transformation, quality control, statistical analysis, visualization, and reporting.

My experience includes more than eight years of R programming, clinically annotated and patient-derived data across oncology and cardiovascular research, and mechanistic studies of protein complexes and proteolytic processing. I work as a connecting professional between clinicians, experimental biologists, statisticians, and computational specialists, converting multidisciplinary questions into executable, documented, and reusable solutions.

## Current Position

**Postdoctoral researcher / Bioinformatician**  
Laboratory of Protease Degradomics and SFB1381 - Dynamic Organization of Cellular Protein Machineries, Faculty of Biology, University of Freiburg  
Supervisor/PI: Prof. Dr. Pitter Huesgen  
April 2024-present

Develop and maintain modular R and Bash pipelines for protein interactions, proteolytic activity, complexome profiling, co-immunoprecipitation proteomics, blue-native mass spectrometry, and shotgun proteomics. Workflows cover data ingestion, transformation, quality control, statistical analysis, visualization, and reporting, using explicit parameters, standardized inputs, Git-based development, HPC environments, and Quarto for reproducibility and project handover.

Served as the group's main bioinformatics-focused scientist, translating discussions with clinicians, experimental scientists, statisticians, and core-facility users into reproducible R analyses. Developed workflows for protein and PTM quantification, terminomics, proteolytic-processing analysis, and clinical multi-omics integration, applying linear models, multivariate methods, missing-data assessment, enrichment analysis, visualization, and reproducible reporting to cohort and longitudinal study designs.

## Skills

- Advanced R programming with more than eight years of experience in data transformation, reusable function and package development, linear modeling, multivariate and exploratory statistics, missing-data assessment, quality control, visualization, and reproducible reporting.
- R, Bash, Bioconductor, Quarto/Markdown, Git/GitHub, GitHub Actions, automated validation, unit testing, structured project organization, and HPC workflows.
- Clinically annotated patient-derived data, clinical-variable integration, cohort and longitudinal analysis, biomarker-oriented exploration, oncology, cardiovascular research, and clinical multi-omics.
- Working Python proficiency for tabular data workflows, scientific prototyping, and lightweight data applications.
- Foundational experience with standardized clinical-trial data concepts, including SDTM/ADaM structures, Tables/Listings/Figures, validation, and source-to-output traceability using public synthetic data.
- Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, including complexome profiling, blue-native MS data analysis workflows, co-immunoprecipitation proteomics, experimental design, sample preparation, TMT and label-free quantification, and proteogenomics.
- Analysis workflows for HPLC-ESI-MS/MS, Q Exactive, timsTOF, FragPipe, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, MaxQuant/MSstats-style outputs, and related proteomics data structures.
